title: Skewed clocks make last write wins keep the wrong value; a Lamport counter fixes the order
captions: Two servers both accept writes. NTP keeps their clocks close, but not equal. Right now, Server B's clock is 3 seconds behind Server A's.
A shop owner sets a price of ₹500 through Server A. Server A stamps the write with its own clock: 10:00:05.
One second later, the owner fixes the price to ₹450. This request lands on Server B. Its slow clock stamps the newer write 10:00:03.
The servers sync and use last write wins. The older write has the bigger timestamp, so both keep ₹500. The newer price is lost, and no error is raised.
Now replay it with Lamport counters. Server A's write gets counter 7. Server B reads the price before it changes it, so it sees 7.
Server B's own counter was lower, so it jumps past 7 and stamps its write 8. The counter follows what B saw, not B's clock. Both servers keep ₹450. This works only because B saw A's write first.
